catalog_quote: Stress in Manihiki is primarily realized as increased intensity or loudness. Manihiki uses right-aligned moraic trochees, where the head foot is to the left. ... A word consisting of only one foot, which is the shortest potential length of a lexical word in Manihiki, will invariably be stressed on the first mora, and thus form what is known in the study of prosody as a trochee. ... [p. 50] Words with three morae in three light syllables ... are invariably stressed on the penultimate syllable ... Words with three morae, where the last two appear together in a heavy syllable ... are stressed on the penultimate mora, not the penultimate syllable, showing that stress in Manihiki is moraic, not syllabic. ... In trimoraic words, where the first two morae together form a heavy syllable, this heavy syllable will be stressed. ... [p. 51] the primary stress of four-mora words fall on the very first mora, so the head foot of a four-mora word must be the one closest to the front, or in other words, the head foot is to the left. ... [pp. 52-53] Most of these [five-mora words] have their main stress on the first mora and their secondary stress on the penultimate mora ... However, if the second syllable is long, this will be the stressed syllable, as seen in (25). This has to be due to the previously mentioned rule of no syllable splitting ... [p. 53] Six-mora words, which have three complete feet with no morae left unfooted, are invariably stressed on the first mora

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (329 pp., text present; title page: 'A Grammar of the Manihiki Language', Aslak Vaag Olesen, MPhil in Linguistics, University of Newcastle NSW, July 2020). I re-extracted pp. 66-74 (printed pp. 48-56) with extracted text and read section 2.6 'Word Stress' in full. Every quoted fragment is present verbatim at the stated locators (the [..] marks elide only list references such as 'are given in (19). As can be seen, they' and the parenthetical 'which is the shortest potential length of a lexical word in Manihiki'): p.48 'Stress in Manihiki is primarily realized as increased intensity or loudness. Manihiki uses right-aligned moraic trochees, where the head foot is to the left.' an…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are parsed into bimoraic trochees aligned to the right edge; primary stress goes on the head of the leftmost foot. Hence: 2-mora words stress the first mora; 3-mora words stress the penultimate mora (initial mora unfooted, unless the first syllable is heavy, which is then stressed); 4- and 6-mora words stress the first mora; 5-mora words stress the first mora (first foot left-aligned) unless the second syllable is long, which then takes stress (no foot may split a syllable). In diphthongs/long vowels the first mora bears the stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Words of at least four morae in at least three syllables carry a secondary stress invariably on the penultimate mora (2.6.7, p. 54); at least one unstressed mora separates primary and secondary.
new_statements.exceptions: 2.6.6 (p. 54): trimoraic manako, tahito, hopenga irregularly stressed on first mora; four-mora inanahi [ˌinaˈnahi] (primary on penultimate mora), tamaiti [taˈmai̯ti], faraoa [faˈɾao̯a] (stress on second-syllable diphthong; faraoa a loan).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/phonological word in citation form; author transcribes isolated words with primary and secondary stress marks; stress realized as intensity; long vowels slightly longer under main stress (fn. to 2.3). No instrumental measurements.
new_statements.identity_note: Olesen describes the single language of Manihiki and Rakahanga atolls (Northern Cook Islands), which he calls 'Manihiki'; consultants recorded in Auckland, Rarotonga and Manihiki. Matches raka1237 (ISO rkh) directly; no dialect split reported. Note Glottolog lists the work as a PhD thesis but the title page says Master of Philosophy (MPhil), July 2020; the repository record is dated 2025.

sources.note: Ch. 2.6 'Word Stress' (pp. 48-55): stress realized mainly as intensity; right-aligned moraic trochees with head foot leftmost; 2-mora words initial, 3-mora words on penultimate mora (or initial heavy syllable), 4- and 6-mora words on first mora with secondary stress on penultimate mora; 5-mora words first mora unless 2nd syllable is long; lists six lexically irregular words (manako, tahito, hopenga, inanahi, tamaiti, faraoa); compares Rarotongan, Rapa Nui, Rapa Iti.

tone.quote: Stress in Manihiki is primarily realized as increased intensity or loudness. Manihiki uses right-aligned moraic trochees, where the head foot is to the left. A foot in the phonological sense consists of either two syllables or two morae. In Manihiki, the mora is the basic prosodic unit, and a foot in Manihiki will thus consist of two morae.
